_note: the Crossing's districts inside the wall. Erik 2026-10-04 asked for the Crossing to look like a big city with its places laid out; the four names in Aevi's mock were placeholders. Now that the twelve roads leave in twelve true directions, each avenue's ward takes its character from the road it lines, the same derivation CCODE-604 used for the quarters outside the gates. Inside the wall the wards are the city's own; outside, the quarters are the road's. Keyed by the foothill each avenue runs to.
principle: The Crossing is every tradition's market, so its wards are the traditions' trades in miniature, arranged by which gate they face. A ward is not a territory and nobody rules it; it is the street a stranger from that direction finds familiar first.

dusklow.name: the Lanternless Ward
dusklow.character: Lamps hooded at dusk by custom, and nobody complains. Umbral traders lodge here, and so do people who would rather not be looked at.

the_low_market.name: the Bargain Ward
the_low_market.character: Pawnshops, bond-brokers and the scribes of the Table of Kept Terms. Everything has a price written on it, including the advice.

the_worn_yard.name: the Breakers' Ward
the_worn_yard.character: Salvage yards and demolition crews. Nothing standing here is older than ten years, and the residents are proud of it.

greyhearth.name: the Grey Ward
greyhearth.character: Undertakers, hospices and the long-houses where the dying wait for a road. The Crossing's dead leave by this gate.

hardline.name: the Drill Ward
hardline.character: Barracks, fencing halls and the Coliseum's training yards. You hear it before you see it: the same command, all day.

longshore.name: the Long Ward
longshore.character: Carters, outfitters and waystations. Everyone leaving the long way buys their boots here, and everyone coming back sells them.

gearsflat.name: the Gear Ward
gearsflat.character: Workshops and smithies under a permanent hum of small engines. Things are mended here that were not meant to be mended.

kindlerow.name: the Kindle Ward
kindlerow.character: Glassworks and lamp-makers. The brightest streets in the city at night, and the hottest by day.

plainstead.name: the Plain Ward
plainstead.character: Notaries, witnesses-for-hire and the courts of record. A promise made in the Plain Ward is written down twice.

stair_hollow.name: the Choir Ward
stair_hollow.character: Chapels, Seraphic hostels and bells on the hour. The ward sings its own name at vespers.

greenmarch.name: the Green Ward
greenmarch.character: Gardens, herbalists and the city's orchards, running up to the edge of Entgrove. The only ward with birds.

thinwater.name: the Thin Ward
thinwater.character: Shrines, hermitages and the quietest streets in the Crossing. People come here to be told nothing, kindly.

_forTheMap: One name per avenue, drawn inside the wall along its avenue in the district style (spaced capitals, faint). The quarter outside the same gate keeps its own character from the road; the ward inside is the city's half of it.
gmMandate: When a scene is in the Crossing, the ward is the texture: say which ward the street is in, and let it be the one facing the way the character came in or is heading out.
